We looked at why, and what it means for the text you set at 12 pixels. Ingrid Solberg Type editor 2 min read Open any recent interface typeface at 12 pixels and put it next to one from ten years ago. The new one is wider. The letters are more open, the spacing is looser, and the x-height has crept up again. Built for the size people read For years, designers drew typefaces at display sizes and let the small sizes take care of themselves. That worked on paper. On screens, small text is where people spend most of their time: labels, captions, table cells, timestamps. The new generation of interface fonts starts at the other end. Designers draw the caption size first, then work up.
